parsed.summary: Lean proves that for every n ≥ 4 there is a polynomial F ∈ ℂ[x_0,…,x_{n-1}] whose quotient ℂ[x]/(F) is ℂ-isomorphic to a polynomial ring in n−1 variables, but which is not a coordinate: no ℂ-automorphism of ℂ[x] sends a variable to F. For n = 4 this is the paper's disproof of the Abhyankar–Sathaye embedding conjecture. The main caveat is that the existential statement omits Theorem 1.1's positive half, namely that f becomes a coordinate after adjoining one variable, so the stable-coordinate counterexample is not formalized. The Lean statement is also stronger than the excerpt: it claims every n ≥ 4, while the paper treats only n = 4.

glossary.decl: MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ ⧸ Ideal.span {F} ≃ₐ[ℂ] MvPolynomial (Fin (n-1)) ℂ
glossary.standard_concept: hypersurface F=0 isomorphic to A^{n-1} (k[x]/(g) ≃ k^{[n-1]})

glossary.plain: F is not a coordinate: no ℂ-algebra automorphism of ℂ[x] maps some variable x_i to F
glossary.standard_concept: coordinate (equivalently, an automorphism sends f to x_1)
glossary.note: Mapping X_i to F is equivalent to the inverse sending F to X_i; any index is allowed, which is the same as the standard notion up to permutation.

lean_claims.plain: For every natural n ≥ 4 there exists F ∈ ℂ[X_0,…,X_{n-1}] such that (i) ℂ[X]/(F) ≅ ℂ[Y_0,…,Y_{n-2}] as ℂ-algebras, and (ii) there is no ℂ-algebra automorphism φ of ℂ[X] and index i with φ(X_i) = F.

paper_claims.plain: For f = x1 − 2Q(Q(x2+x4)+x1x4), Q = x2²−x4²+x1x3, in ℂ[x1..x4]: some ℂ-automorphism of R[w] sends f to x1, but no ℂ-automorphism of R does.
For every λ ∈ ℂ, f^{-1}(λ) ≅ A^3 and its embedding in A^4 is not rectifiable. This disproves the Abhyankar–Sathaye conjecture in dimension 4.

coverage.why: Only the non-coordinate half is stated, existentially. The one-stable-coordinate part (automorphism of R[w]) is absent.
At n=4 Lean gives one hypersurface (F=0) ≅ A^3 that is not a coordinate, i.e. the AS-conjecture disproof. It does not cover every λ-fiber or the specific f.
Lean claims counterexamples in all dimensions ≥ 4; the excerpt only treats n = 4. The paper's f becomes a coordinate after adding a variable, so it does not directly give n=5.

flags.explanation: The stable-coordinate half of Theorem 1.1 (f is a coordinate of R[w]) is not formalized. The headline counterexample to the stable coordinate conjecture is therefore not checked. Only the Abhyankar–Sathaye counterexample is.
flags.probe_idea: Add the conjunct: ∃ φ : MvPolynomial (Fin (n+1)) ℂ ≃ₐ[ℂ] MvPolynomial (Fin (n+1)) ℂ, ∃ i, φ (X i) = rename Fin.castSucc F.

flags.explanation: The statement is existential and does not pin down the paper's explicit degree-5 polynomial f, nor all fibers f−λ.
flags.probe_idea: State the theorem for the explicit f at n=4 and for f - C λ for arbitrary λ.

flags.explanation: Lean claims the result for every n ≥ 4, which is stronger than the n=4 result in the excerpt. Higher-dimensional cases are not in the excerpt. Stronger is acceptable, but this content goes beyond the paper.

lint_verdicts.why: Since hn : 4 ≤ n, n - 1 is the true predecessor and no truncation occurs.
